correctness.rationale: Use B_n=P_{2n}/2 and C_n=Q_{2n}. The Pell square identities reduce sums of k consecutive squares to (B_k Q_{4n+2k+2}-k)/16 and (B_k Q_{4n+2k+2}+k)/2 respectively. Consecutive block differences and strong divisibility of Pell numbers give gcd of B-square differences B_k, and gcd of C-square differences 8B_k. For odd k, B_k odd and relevant residue modulo 4 makes C initial block sum odd, giving both gcds gcd(B_k,k). Independently regenerated sequences and verified direct 9-window GCDs for every odd k<=101. The proof uses infinite GCD of successive differences, not bounded windows.
